source:
Act as an Expert Roblox Developer. Discard previous modern UI concepts. We are building a game focused on PHYSICAL character movement, CLASSIC ROBLOX visual style (Stud textures), and 100% Mobile Touch Support.

[CORE GAMEPLAY & WORLD (WALKING AROUND)]
- The player MUST physically walk around the world. Create a spawn point on a green baseplate.
- Create a physical Shop Stall model in the Workspace.
- Add a ProximityPrompt to the stall (ActionText: "Open Shop"). 
- The shop UI ONLY opens when the player walks up to the stall and interacts. Include a script that automatically closes the UI if the player walks too far away.

[CLASSIC UI RECREATION (Based exactly on 51141.jpg)]
- Build a ScreenGui named "RetroShopGui". It MUST be fully Mobile Supported (use UIAspectRatioConstraint and Scale sizing so it fits perfectly on all phone screens).
- Main UI Frame: Brown background with the classic Roblox "Stud" decal texture applied.
- Header Frame: Bright Green background with the "Stud" texture.
- Header Elements: 
 1. TextLabel: "New seeds In [Timer]s" (Use a Retro/Arcade font, white text with black outline).
 2. Yellow TextButton: "RESTOCK" (Red text).
 3. Red TextButton: "X" (Close button).
- Body: A ScrollingFrame containing the seed items.
- Item Template (Inside ScrollingFrame):
 - 3D ViewportFrame or ImageLabel showing a blocky seed (e.g., Orange block for Carrot).
 - TextLabel: Item Name ("Carrot Seed", "Strawberry Seed") in bold white text.
 - TextLabel: Stock left ("X23 Stock") in grey text.
 - TextLabel: Price ("10¢", "50¢") in bright green text.
 - TextButton: Rarity label ("Common") with a grey gradient background.

[STRICT MOBILE SUPPORT]
- Ensure the player's movement joystick and jump buttons are NEVER blocked by the UI.
- All UI buttons must have a large enough touch radius for mobile thumbs.

Write the complete Luau code to generate this exact retro UI structure, apply the stud textures, handle the ProximityPrompt for physical walking interaction, and enforce mobile UI scaling!

answers.ask: How much ground should the baseplate cover - just enough to walk up to the stall, or a full-sized baseplate with room to build on later?
answers.answer: Use a small baseplate, just large enough for the player to spawn and physically walk up to the shop stall; this is a focused playable vertical slice.

config.addendum:
LAYOUT FEATURES for this Simulation map. Build these as the actual structure of the space rather than as set dressing, keep them visually distinct from one another, and keep the whole layout legible in one view.

SHAPE OF THE SPACE - Shared Persistent World: No personal plot at all — one common world everybody operates in together.

INCLUDE:
- Upgrades Bazaar: The central storefront zone — eggs, upgrades, progression shops — that every player has to keep coming back to.
- Progression Circulation: Walkable or drivable circulation chaining the hub to wherever value is actually produced.
